notes: Pass 3 target: the sub-450/month tail that the pass 2 `esim` sweeps could not reach in de-de, fr-fr, it-it and es-es because they hit the API row limit, plus the en-us mid and long tail that was never swept beyond 5 head terms.

Method: keywords-explorer-matching-terms, match_mode=terms, order_by=volume:desc, with a volume floor of 10 on every call. For de-de, en-gb, it-it, es-es and fr-fr an upper bound of 440 was also applied so units were spent on the uncollected tail rather than re-buying heads that passes 1 and 2 already hold. en-us used no upper bound below 1500 because only 196 US rows existed in total.
Every volume and cpc in this file is a raw Ahrefs figure. Nothing is estimated, interpolated or invented. cpc is in USD cents as the API returns it.

difficulty is null throughout. Ahrefs charges 10 units per row for it on top of the 13 unit base, which would have cost 43 percent of the budget. The consolidation script does not read difficulty, so the units bought roughly 1,300 extra real keywords instead. Difficulty can be backfilled on a shortlist later at 10 units a row.

intent is derived from the keyword text, not from the Ahrefs intents object, which is also a paid column. Research-shaped queries (how/what/which/welche/quelle/cual, plus review, erfahrungen, avis, recensioni, vergleich) are informational; everything else carrying a destination, a regional token or a commercial modifier is commercial.

111 fetched rows were discarded as not addressable travel demand: Holafly and Ubigi product-page titles that Ahrefs indexes as keywords (for example "esim europe unlimited data - holafly", 3,600/mo), US domestic carrier prepaid queries (att/verizon/t-mobile prepaid esim), free-trial and free-government-esim hunting, "esim <country> news" rows, and concatenated product-grid fragments. Together they carried about 49,900 monthly searches that this file deliberately does not claim.
142 fetched rows were already present in one of the three earlier files and 44 were duplicates inside this pass. Both were dropped before counting.

Honest caveat on quality: a visible slice of the German and French tail is programmatically generated aggregator vocabulary ("esim promo-code marokko", "virtuelles esim indonesien", "esim regional egypte", each around 50-70/mo). The volumes are real Ahrefs figures but the pattern suggests one competitor has spun up a template page set per country per modifier. These are genuine travel-shaped queries and are kept, but they should be treated as thin, low-confidence demand rather than as evidence of strong independent search behaviour.
Budget: 35,187 of the 40,000 units allowed were spent. Collection stopped there rather than padding the file with lower-relevance sweeps.
